ऋद्धिमत्: Ṛddhimant: A big serpent (महानाग), living in a lake on the Gandhamādana mountain 3. 157. 1, 14. Carried away by Suparṇa; the spectacle seen by the Pāṇḍavas 3. 157. 14-15.
ऋद्धिमन्त्: Ṛddhimant: A big serpent (महानाग), living in a lake on the Gandhamādana mountain 3. 157. 1, 14. Carried away by Suparṇa; the spectacle seen by the Pāṇḍavas 3. 157. 14-15.
ऋषभ: Ṛṣabha: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, offered in the सर्पसत्र; described as ‘fast as wind’ (वातवेग), ‘having excess of poison’ (विषोल्बण) 1. 52. 16, 1, 13.

Ṛṣabha1 m.: Name of a mountain. A. Location: Situated in the Pāṇḍya country (पाण्ड्येषु) 3. 83. 19, close to the ocean (सागरोरसि) 5. 110. 22. B. Des-cription: Worshipped by gods (सुरपूजित) 3. 83. 19. C. Importance: A visit to the mountain Ṛṣabha secures for the visitor the fruit of the Vājapeya sacrifice and he (after death) rejoices in the heaven (नाक-पृष्ठे च मोदते) 3. 83. 19. D. My-thological event: Suparṇa told Gālava that after eating and resting on the Ṛṣabha mountain they would go back from the mountain 5. 110. 22; when the two of them reached the summit of the mountain they saw there the Brāhmaṇī Śāṇḍilī engaged in austerities 5. 111. 1.
Ṛṣabha2 m.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated in Kośalā; by visiting the तीर्थ and by fasting there for three nights (त्रिरात्रो-पोषितः) one gets the fruit of the Vājapeya sacrifice 3. 83. 10.
ऋग्वेद: Ṛgveda m.: Name of one of the four Vedic Saṃhitās. A. Relationship with Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa: Nārāyaṇa, the greatest of the gods (देव-देव 3. 186. 129), told the sage Mārkaṇḍeya that the Ṛgveda and the other Vedas arise from him and enter into him (मत्तः प्रादुर्भवन्त्य् एते माम् एव प्रविशन्ति च) 3. 187. 14; Bhagavān (Kṛṣṇa) told Arjuna that in the Ṛgveda and in many other texts his names have been enumerated by great sages (ऋग्वेदे … बहूनि मम नामानि कीर्तितानि महर्षिभिः) 12. 328. 8-9; those versed in the Vedas call Bhagavān as the Ṛgveda of twentyone branches (एकविंशति-शाखं च ऋग्वेदं मां प्रचक्षते । … ये वै वेदविदो जनाः) 12. 330. 32. B. Source of mythology and व्रतस्: Gṛtsamada, son of Vītahavya, who in appearance was like another Indra, was once caught hold of by the Daityas; this incident is referred to in the Ṛgveda (cf. ṚV. 2. 12) where Gṛtsa-mada is glorified by the Brāhmaṇas (ऋग्वेदे वर्तते चाग्र्या श्रुतिर् अत्र विशां पते यत्र गृत्समदो ब्रह्मन् ब्राह्मणैः स महीयते) 13. 31. 56; a व्रत called Trisau-parṇavrata, difficult to observe, is found in the Ṛgveda (ऋग्वेदपाठपठितं व्रतम् एतद् धि दुश्चरम्) 12. 336. 20. C. Ṛgveda personified: (1) Ṛgveda, along with the Sāmaveda and the Purāṇas, move in front of the chariot of Mahādeva to protect it (when Śiva got ready to fight with the Tripuras) 8. 24. 80; (2) Ṛgveda together with the other three Vedas, visit the Sabhā of Brahmadeva (2. 11. 19) and wait on him 2. 11. 23, 31; (3) Ṛgveda, adorned with क्रम and पद, came to the sacrifice of Mahādeva (Śiva) who had assumed the form of Varuṇa 13. 85. 4, 2. [See Ṛc]
ऋच्: Ṛc f. (mostly plural): Often stands for the Ṛgveda or stanzas in it; in such contexts Ṛc often occurs along with Yajus and Sāman. A. Number: their number given as ten thousand (दशेदम् ऋक्सहस्राणि) 12. 238. 14 (दश किंचिदधिकानि ऋक्सहस्राणि) Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 246. 14). B. Their study recommended and their chanting referred to: the Brāhmaṇas are enjoined to study the ऋच्स्, the यजुसेस् and the सामन्स् (सर्वान् वेदान् अधीयीत … ऋचो यजूंषि सामानि) 12. 243. 2; 12. 260. 36; these are to be studied with due respect for the teacher; hence, while taking an oath to prove his innocence, Bharadvāja said: “who steals the lotus-stalks, may he study ऋच्स् and यजुसेस् disrespecting his teacher” (उपाध्या-यम् अधः कृत्वा ऋचो ऽध्येतु यजूंषि च ।  … बिसस्तैन्यं करोति यः) 13. 95. 62; a Brāhmaṇa who can recite the ऋच्स्, the यजुसेस् and sing the सामन्स् is considered to be the proper person to receive gifts (ऋग्यजुःसामगो विद्वान् … पात्रम् उच्यते) 12. 297. 15; such a learned Brāhmaṇa is to be honoured as a god (ऋग्यजुःसामविद् पूज्यो नित्यं स्याद् देववद् द्विजः) 12. 60. 42; Brāhmaṇas, ac-companying the Pāṇḍavas to the Dvaitavana, recited ऋच्स्, यजुसेस्, and सामन्स् (यजुषां ऋचां च साम्नां च … आसीद् उच्चार्यमा-णानाम् निस्वनो हृदयंगमः) 3. 27. 3; those who had studied the ऋच्स्, recited them according to the पद- and the क्रम-पाठ in the sacrificial rites performed in Kaṇva's hermitage (ऋचो बह्वृचमुख्यैश् च प्रेर्-यमाणाः पदक्रमैः । शुष्राव … विततेष्व् इह कर्मसु) 1. 64. 31; one should study त्रयी विद्या (threefold knowledge), detailed in the Vedas, from ऋच्, यजुस्, सामन्, and अथर्वन् (त्रयीविद्याम् अवेक्षेत वेदेषूक्ताम् अथाङ्गतः । ऋक्सामवर्णाक्षरतो यजुषो ऽथर्वणस् तथा) 12. 227. 1. C. Their importance for Dharmaśāstra and Adhyātma-śāstra: the शास्त्र, consisting of a hundred thousand श्लोकस्, produced by the seven sages, Marīci, Atri and others (12. 322. 26-27), and which is approved by the ऋच्स्, यजुसेस् and सामन्स्, as well as by the अथर्वाङ्गिरसस् will be the source of धर्म (कृतं शतसहस्रं हि श्लोकानाम् इदम् उत्तमम् । … प्रवृत्तौ च निवृत्तौ च योनिर् एतद् भविष्यति । ऋग्यजुःसामभिर् जुष्टम् अथर्वाङ्गिरसैस् तथा ॥ ) 12. 322. 36-37; Bhagavān (Kṛṣṇa) identifies himself with ऋच्, सामन् and यजुस् (अहम् … ऋक् साम यजुर् एव च) 6. 31. 17; the शास्त्र constituting the secret of all the Vedas and leading to the knowledge of आत्मन् was churned out like nectar from the ten thou-sand ऋच्स् (रहस्यं सर्ववेदानां … आत्म-प्रत्ययिकं शास्त्रं … दशेदम् ऋक्सह-स्राणि निर्मथ्यामृतम् उद्धृतम्) 12. 238. 13-14; there is only one सामन्, one यजुस् and one ऋच् (एकं साम यजुर् एकम् ऋग् एका) 12. 60. 45 (Nī. on 12. 60. 47 Bom. Ed. अकारो वै सर्वा वाक् … इति श्रुतेर् एकम् अकाररूपम् एव अक्षरं यथा सामादिरू-पम्). D. Their use and importance for rites (real or metaphorical): ऋच्स् and सामन्स् were chanted at the cremation rites of those fallen in the war (साम्नां ऋचां च नादेन) 11. 26. 40; those who know Nārāyaṇa recite ऋच्स् (= stanzas as holy ऋच्स् ?) to the effect that when formerly animals were bound for the god Nārāyaṇa सामन्स् were sung 14. 25. 16-17 (Nī. on 14. 25. 16 Bom. Ed.: ऋचः ‘तप आसीद् गृहपतिर्’ (Tai. Br. 3. 12. 9. 3) इत्याद्याः … शंसन्ति योगयज्ञे प्रमाणत्वेन कथयन्ति तैत्तिरी-यादयः । नारायणविदः वेदविद आत्मविदो वा । नारायणाय आत्मप्राप्त्यर्थं यत् यदा पशून् इन्द्रियाणि अविन्दन् वश्यत्वेन प्राप्तवन्तः); a sacrifice has seventeen constituents three of which are ऋच्स्, यजुसेस् and सामन्स् (ऋचो यजूंषि सामानि … अङ्गान्य् एतानि यज्ञस्य) 12. 260. 26. E. Ṛcs used for praising various deities: In this context ऋच् does not always mean a stanza from the Ṛgveda, but also one similar to it, or a stanza in general: (1) Excellent Brāh-maṇas praised Indra with praises consisting of ऋच्स्, यजुसेस् and सामन्स् (स्तूयमानं द्विजाग्र्यैश् च ऋग्यजुःसामसंस्तवैः) 3. 44. 18; (2) son of Ṛcīka (Śunaḥśepa), having praised with ऋच्स् gods who receive shares in sacrifices, became Viśvāmitra's son (ऋग्भिः स्तुत्वा महाभागो देवान् वै यज्ञभागिनः) 12. 281. 13; (3) various sages (Asita Devala and others 12. 281. 15-16) praised Viṣṇu with ऋच्स् and obtained सिद्धि by practising तपस् due to his favour (स्तुत्वा विष्णुम् ऋग्भिः) 12. 281. 17; (4) Vyāsa, his pupils, and his son Śuka praised Hari with ऋच्स् from all the four Vedas (स चास्माकम् उपाध्यायः सहास्माभिर् विशां पते । चतुर्वेदोद्गताभिश् च ऋग्भिस् तम् अभितुष्टुवे) 12. 327. 100; Vyāsa and other sages worshipped Kṛṣṇa with praises consi-sting of ऋच्स्, यजुसेस् and सामन्स् (ऋग्यजुः-सामसंयुक्तैर् वचोभिः कृष्णम् अर्चयन्) 12. 52. 22; sages praised Madhusūdana with praises adorned with the contents of ऋच्स् (वाग्भिर् ऋग्भूषितार्थाभिः) 13. 126. 46; (5) Upamanyu, as directed by his teacher Dhaumya, praised Aśvins with the ऋच् stanzas (1. 3. 60-70 which actually are not from the Ṛgveda) to regain his eye-sight (वाग्भिर् ऋग्भिः) 1. 3. 59; (6) Śiva is praised with ऋच्स् in Tantric rites by those who are versed in the Ṛgveda (ऋग्भिर् यम् अनुशंसन्ति तन्त्रे कर्मणि बह्वृचः) (? बह्वृचाः)) 13. 16. 48; sages praised goddess Umā with praises adorned with the contents of the ऋच्स् (वाग्भिर् ऋग्भूषितार्था-भिः) 13. 128. 24. F. Their importance and utility limited: Sage Sanatsujāta told Dhṛtarāṣṭra that the छन्दस् (ऋच्), यजुस् and सामन् did not save one from sin 5. 43. 1-3; the ऋच्स्, the सामन्स् and the यजुसेस् have a beginning and therefore an end i. e. they are not eternal (12. 199. 16-18); the अक्षर पद is not to be found in the ऋच्स्, यजुसेस्, अथर्वन्स्, and सामन्स् 5. 44. 21; even after studying the collections of the ऋच्स् and the सामन्स्, and the यजुसेस् Bṛhaspati did not know the source of beings (ऋक्सामसंघांश् च यजूंषि चाहम् … अधीत्य … भूतप्रकृइत्ं न वेद्मि) 12. 194. 8; mortals who believed in non-distinction (between ब्रह्मन् and आत्मन्) having seen that the ऋच्स्, the सामन्स्, the यजुसेस् and the prosperity desired (through them) was something distinct (from the highest self) (resorted) to तपस् by practising austerities (अपृथग्धर्मिणो मर्त्या ऋक्सामानि यजूंषि च । काम्यां पुष्टिम् पृथग् दृष्ट्वा तपोभिस् तप एव च) 12. 224. 63 (अद्वैतनिष्ठा मर्त्यास् तप एव योगम् एव कृतयुगे ऽनुतिष्ठन्तीति शेषः । ऋगादीनि काम्या इष्टीश् च … पृथक् तपोभिर् आलोचनैः दृष्ट्वा … तत् परित्यज्य योगपरा एव बभूवुर् इत्य् अर्थः Nī. on Bom. Ed. 12. 232. 33); also cf. तपोयज्ञा द्विजातयः 12. 224. 61; all those who see the non-distinction (between पौरुष कर्म दैव, and स्वभाव 12. 230. 4-5), keep away (दृष्ट्वा = कृत्वा) their love and hatred for ऋच्स्, सामन्स् and यजुसेस्, and practise तपस् in the Kṛta age (अपृथग्दर्शिनः सर्वे ऋक्सामसु यजुःषु च । कामद्वेशौ पृथग् दृष्ट्वा तपः कृत उपासते) 12. 230. 8 (Nī. however, on Bom. Ed. 12. 238. 8: वेदत्रये ऽपि भेदम् अपश्यन्तः काम्यादीन् (? कामादीन्) पृथक्कृत्य तपो ज्ञानम् उपासते श्रयन्ति). [See Ṛgveda]
ऋषिवंश: Ṛṣivaṃśa m.: Name of a passage in the Anuśāsanaparvan listing the names of sages and also of kings, some of whom are royal sages (राजर्षि) 13. 151. 30-51. The names of sages, rich in austerities, who having practised austerities had attained perfection (विप्रांस् तपःसिद्धांस् तपोधि-कान् 13. 151. 30) are listed according to the quarters they occupy: Yavakrīta, Raibhya, Kakṣīvān and some others in the east; Ulmucu, Pramucu, Mumucu and some others in the south; Uṣadgu and his brothers, Parivyādha, Dīrghatamas and some others in the west; Atri, Vasiṣṭha, Śakti and some others in the north 13. 151. 31-40; the recitation of the Ṛṣivaṃśa, along with that of the Daivatavaṃśa, at two twilights is very effective in removing sins (द्विसं-ध्यं पठितः पुत्र कल्मषापहरः परः) 13. 151. 2; (कीर्तितान् … सर्वपापप्र-मोचनान्) 13. 151. 30; then follow names of kings beginning with Nṛga and ending with Kakṣasena 13. 151. 41-50; some of these kings are royal sages, viz. Mucakunda (राजर्षिः) 13. 151. 46; Śveta (राजर्षिसत्-तमः) 13. 151. 47, Kṣupa (राजर्षिः) 13. 151. 48, Nala (राजर्षिः) 13. 151. 49, and Kakṣasena (राजर्षिः) 13. 151. 50; the list is apparently intended to be recited by one who does not wish to meet with difficulties, nor incur sin, nor encounter enemies, and by one who wishes to have sure victory and great happiness after death (मा विघ्नं मा च मे पापं मा च मे परिपन्थिनः । ध्रुवो जयो मे नित्यं स्यात् परत्र च परा गतिः) 13. 151. 51.
ऋक्षवत्: Ṛkṣavant m.: Name of a mountain (lit. ‘where bears abound’). A. Kulaparvata: Listed by Saṃjaya among the seven Kulaparvatas (principal ranges of mountains) of the Bhāratavarṣa 6. 10. 10. B. Location: Nala told Dama-yantī that many roads beyond the moun-tain Ṛkṣavant lead to the Dakṣiṇāpatha (एते गच्छन्ति बहवः पन्थानो दक्षिणा-पथम् । अवन्तीम् ऋक्षवन्तं च समति-क्रम्य पर्वतम् ॥ ) 3. 58. 20. C. Past event: Son of Viḍūratha, a descendant of the Pauravas (पौरवदायादः), was one of the few Kṣatriyas saved during their slaughter by Rāma Jāmadagnya; he was reared by the bears on this mountain (ऋक्षैः संवर्धितो विप्र ऋक्षवत्य् एव पर्वते) 12. 49. 67. D. Simile: The army of the Pāṇḍavas moving (in two divisions) in front and at the back of the chariots of Kṛṣṇa and the Pāṇḍavas resembled the river Narmadā flowing (in two streams) in front and at the back of the mountain after meeting it 12. 52. 32.
ऋक्षवन्त्: Ṛkṣavant m.: Name of a mountain (lit. ‘where bears abound’). A. Kulaparvata: Listed by Saṃjaya among the seven Kulaparvatas (principal ranges of mountains) of the Bhāratavarṣa 6. 10. 10. B. Location: Nala told Dama-yantī that many roads beyond the moun-tain Ṛkṣavant lead to the Dakṣiṇāpatha (एते गच्छन्ति बहवः पन्थानो दक्षिणा-पथम् । अवन्तीम् ऋक्षवन्तं च समति-क्रम्य पर्वतम् ॥ ) 3. 58. 20. C. Past event: Son of Viḍūratha, a descendant of the Pauravas (पौरवदायादः), was one of the few Kṣatriyas saved during their slaughter by Rāma Jāmadagnya; he was reared by the bears on this mountain (ऋक्षैः संवर्धितो विप्र ऋक्षवत्य् एव पर्वते) 12. 49. 67. D. Simile: The army of the Pāṇḍavas moving (in two divisions) in front and at the back of the chariots of Kṛṣṇa and the Pāṇḍavas resembled the river Narmadā flowing (in two streams) in front and at the back of the mountain after meeting it 12. 52. 32.
ऋश्यमूक: Ṛśyamūka m.: Name of a mountain (once spelt Ṛṣyamūka 3. 26. 8). A. Description: Having many roots and fruit (बहुमूलफलं गिरिम्) 3. 264. 9. B. Events from the Rāmāyaṇa: Gandharva Viśvāvasu informed Rāma about the mountain Ṛśyamūka: by its side lay the lake Pampā; Sugrīva, with his four coun-sellors, lived on that mountain 3. 263. 40-41; Hanūmant also told Bhīma that he lived for a long time on the Ṛśyamūka mountain with Sugrīva after the latter was offended by Vālin 3. 147. 27; Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa saw the five monkey chiefs seated on the summit of this mountain 3. 264. 9; 3. 147. 31; the sage Mārkaṇḍeya saw Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa on the peak of the Ṛṣyamūka 3. 26. 8.
ऋषभकूट: Ṛṣabhakūṭa m.: Name of a mountain. An ascetic by name Ṛṣabha, hundreds of years old, lived there (which probably explains the name) 3. 109. 7. [See Hemakūṭa]
ऋषभद्वीप: Ṛṣabhadvīpa m.: Name of a holy island (a तीर्थ). A. Location: On the river Sarasvatī 3. 82. 139; Sarasvatī is known as Suveṇu near Ṛṣabhadvīpa where Sarasvatī arrived for king Kuru who was offering a sacrifice at Kurukṣetra (सुवेणुर् ऋषभद्वीपे) 9. 37. 24. B. Description: Holy (पुण्य) and visited by royal sages (राजर्षिसेवित) 9. 37. 24; fit to be resorted to (सेव्य) 3. 82. 139; the killer of Krauñcas (?) (क्रौञ्चनिषूदन) 3. 82. 139. C. Importance: If one bathes in Sarasvatī at this island he shines in a विमान (विमानस्थो विराजते) 3. 82. 139.
ऋषिकुल्या: Ṛṣikulyā1 f.: Name of a तीर्थ। If one bathes in the Ṛṣikulyā and if one lives there for a month subsisting only on vegetables (शाकाहारः) he reaches the world of the Ṛṣis (ऋषिलोकं प्रपद्यते) 3. 82. 44, 43.

Ṛṣikulyā2 f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people use its water for drinking purposes 6. 10. 34, 13; all the rivers listed here are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for cita-tion see Atikṛṣṇā); finds mention in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 21, 2; [ऋषिकुल्याः (pl.) 2. 25. 4: probably not a proper name; when Arjuna went beyond the Śveta moun-tain and ran over the Hāṭaka country, he saw the lake Mānasa and many small rivers of the Ṛṣis (ऋषिकुल्याश् च ताः सर्वा ददर्श … )].
ऋषिगिरि: Ṛṣigiri m.: Name of a mountain. One of the five mountains surrounding the city Girivraja in the Magadha country; the mountains came together as though for protecting the city (रक्षन्तीवाभिसंहत्य  … गिरिव्रजम्) 2. 19. 3; all the five moun-tains are described as shining (शुभाः), hav-ing high peaks (महाशृङ्गाः), shady trees (शीतलद्रुमाः), and of solid body (सं-हताङ्गाः) 2. 19. 2-3; they were as though concealed by forests of fragrant and attractive Lodhra trees whose branches were covered with flowers 2. 19. 4.
ऋश्यशृङ्गस्य: Ṛśyaśṛṅgasya āśramaḥ m.: Name of the hermitage of Ṛśyaśṛṅga. Situated near the lake Mahāhrada; described as holy (पुण्य) and beautifying the lake (महाह्रदं शोभयन्) 3. 113. 25. [See Kāśyapāśrama]
ऋषिक: Ṛṣika m. (pl.): Name of a country and its people. A. Location: In the north (प्रययाव् उत्तरां दिशम्) 2. 24. 1; specified as nor-thern Ṛṣikas (ऋषिकान् उत्तरान् अपि) 2. 24. 24. B. Description: Great Ṛṣikas (परमर्-षिक°) 2. 24. 25. C. Epic events: (1) Arjuna in his expedition to the north before the Rājasūya conquered the northern Ṛṣikas; in the Ṛṣika country there was a battle between Arjuna and Ṛṣikas as terrible as the one (between gods) and Tārakāsura (?); Arjuna collected from them as tribute eight horses looking like a parrot's belly, some others looking like peacocks, and still others having the qualities of both (ऋषिकान् उत्तरान् अपि । … व्यजयत् पाकशासनिः ॥ ऋषिकेषु तु संग्रामो बभूवातिभयंकरः । तारका-मयसंकाशः परमर्षिकपार्थयोः ॥ स विजित्य ततो राजन्न् ऋषिकान् … । शुकोदर-समप्रख्यान् हयान् अष्टौ समानयत् । मयूरसदृशान् अन्यान् उभयान् एव चाप-रान् ॥ ) 2. 24. 24-26; (2) Drupada men-tioned Ṛṣikas among those kings and peoples to whom messengers were to be sent to seek their help in war (काम्बोजा ऋषिका ये च) 5. 4. 15; (एतेषां प्रेष्यतां शीघ्रम्) 5. 4. 25; (3) Dhṛtarāṣṭra men-tioned among Karṇa's exploits his victory over Ṛṣikas and his making them pay tribute (अश्मकान् ऋषिकाम्स् तथा । यो जित्वा समरे वीरश् चक्रे बलिभृतः पुरा ॥ ) 8. 5. 20.
